title: VISTA views Messier 78
caption: The star-forming region Messier 78, imaged by ESO's VISTA telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Blue patches of reflected light, dark streams of dust and red jets fill this detailed view of Messier 78, a star-forming region in the constellation Orion, the Hunter.

Each feature has a different origin. The blue regions are dust clouds reflecting the light of hot young stars, in the same way that mist glows around a lamp. The dark streams are thicker dust that blocks the light from behind. The red jets are the most revealing, because they come from stars still in the process of forming, which fling out narrow streams of material as they grow.

The image was taken with VISTA, an infrared survey telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. Infrared light can pass through dust that hides young stars at visible wavelengths, so VISTA can show jets and newborn stars that visible-light images miss.

understand.summary: VISTA's VIRCAM camera imaged Messier 78 in near-infrared light through Z, Y, J, H and Ks filters. The color mapping isn't published.
